question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis?

options.A: To kill all viruses while leaving bacteria alive
options.B: To reduce the total number of common bacteria
options.C: To eliminate every single microorganism and spore
options.D: To remove visible dirt and grease from the skin

explanation: You've got this! Surgical asepsis is all about absolute sterility—getting rid of every living germ and tough spore so nothing can cause infection. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h1)

question: How is surgical asepsis different from medical asepsis?

options.A: Surgical asepsis completely eliminates microorganisms, while medical asepsis only reduces their number.
options.B: Medical asepsis requires sterile gloves, while surgical asepsis uses clean non-sterile gloves.
options.C: Surgical asepsis is used only in the ward, while medical asepsis is used in the operating room.
options.D: Medical asepsis destroys spores, while surgical asepsis only targets active bacteria.

explanation: Think of medical asepsis (like handwashing) as cleaning things up for everyday safety, while surgical asepsis is the total knockout—complete sterility for deep tissues! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h1)

question: In which zone of the surgical suite can staff members wear regular street clothes?
explanation: The unrestricted zone is the welcome area where you enter before changing into your scrubs. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: You walk into the main operating room where a patient's abdomen is open. What must you wear in this restricted zone?

options.A: An isolation gown and sterile gloves only
options.B: Surgical scrubs, head cover, and a surgical mask
options.C: Clean street clothes with a disposable plastic apron
options.D: A lab coat worn over casual clothes

explanation: When heading into the restricted zone, full theatre gear (scrubs, cap, and mask) is a must to keep stray hairs and respiratory droplets away from the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the water drain off your arms?

options.A: From the elbows down toward the fingertips
options.B: Directly off the sides of the forearms
options.C: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.D: Upward toward the shoulders using towels

explanation: Always let water flow from your cleanest area (fingertips) down to your elbows. Gravity is your friend here! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h3)

question: After scrubbing up, why do you keep your hands raised up as you walk to the operating room?

options.A: To prevent water and soapy residue from flowing backward from the elbows onto the hands
options.B: To allow visual inspection of the fingernails for remaining debris
options.C: To dry the skin faster under the air current of the operating room vents
options.D: To make it easier for the circulator nurse to open sterile gown packages

explanation: Keeping your hands higher than your elbows ensures dirty water drips away from your freshly scrubbed hands, keeping them safe. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h3)

question: How wide is the standard unsterile border around a sterile drape or package wrapper?
explanation: That outer one-inch edge of any sterile wrap is considered touched and unsterile. Good rule of thumb to always remember! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: A surgical instrument slips from your hand and lands partially on the edge of the instrument table tray. What should you do?

options.A: Consider the instrument contaminated and discard it immediately.
options.B: Wipe the instrument with an alcohol swab before using it again.
options.C: Inspect the instrument to see if it touched the floor.
options.D: Use the instrument quickly before air contaminants settle on it.

explanation: When in doubt, throw it out! Touching that unsterile edge means the tool is no longer safe for the sterile field. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h4)

question: When cleaning a patient's skin before surgery, what is the correct way to apply the antiseptic solution?

options.A: Starting at the incision site and scrubbing outward in circles
options.B: Starting at the outer edges and wiping inward toward the center
options.C: Wiping vertically from top to bottom regardless of the incision line
options.D: Scrubbing firmly back and forth across the entire wound in straight lines

explanation: Always start clean (the incision area) and work your way out. This way, you don't drag dirt and germs from the outer skin back into the cut! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why are prophylactic antibiotics usually given within one hour before the surgical incision is made?

options.A: To allow the surgical team time to perform hand scrubbing rituals
options.B: To neutralize any bacteria already present in the circulating air
options.C: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea while on the operating table
options.D: To ensure peak tissue concentration of the drug when the skin is opened

explanation: Timing is everything! Giving the drug right before surgery means the antibiotic is fully active in the tissues the exact second the skin opens. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h5)

question: Who is primarily responsible for keeping track of surgical instruments and sponges in the operating room?

options.A: The anaesthetist and the operating room manager
options.B: The lead surgeon and the assistant surgeon
options.C: The circulator nurse and the scrub nurse
options.D: The central sterile supply department technician

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! The scrub nurse and circulator nurse double-team the counts to make sure nothing is left behind. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h6)

question: You notice a surgeon accidentally touches their non-sterile mask with a gloved hand during a procedure. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Politely inform the surgeon of the break in technique and ensure the gloves are changed
options.B: Assume the gloves are still clean because the mask was recently put on
options.C: Ask the circulating nurse to document the event in the patient's chart
options.D: Wait until the end of the operation to mention the incident to the head nurse

explanation: Patient safety is everyone's job. Speak up kindly and immediately if sterility is broken so the team can fix it right away! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h6)
